scenes.heading: Human impacts on ecosystems
scenes.sub: How we change the living world, and how to protect it
scenes.say: Humans change ecosystems more than any other species. Australia has many species found nowhere else, so knowing the threats, and how to reduce them, really matters. Remember the big four: hip C. Habitat loss, introduced species, pollution and climate change.
scenes.caption: Humans change ecosystems more than any other species. Australia has many species found nowhere else, so knowing the threats, and how to reduce them, really matters. Remember the big four: HIP-C. Habitat loss, introduced species, pollution and climate change.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A party split into rooms with locked doors
scenes.science: Habitat fragmentation isolates small populations in bush patches
scenes.breaks: guests can still text each other, but isolated populations can't share genes unless animals physically move between patches.
scenes.say: Habitat fragmentation is like a party where most doors get locked. Guests are stuck in small rooms, some run out of snacks, and they only meet the same few people. Small isolated populations lose genetic diversity. A wildlife corridor is like unlocking a hallway.

scenes.heading: Introduced species
points: Left their predators and diseases behind
Natives have no defences against them
Cane toads poison quolls and goannas
Rabbits compete, eat seedlings, cause erosion
scenes.say: Introduced species often thrive because they left their predators, parasites and diseases behind, and native species have no defences. Cane toads poison native predators like quolls and goannas. Rabbits compete with bilbies and wombats, eat seedlings and cause soil erosion.

scenes.heading: Eutrophication
scenes.say: In eutrophication, fertiliser washes into a lake and algae grow rapidly. When the algae die, decomposer bacteria break them down and use up the dissolved oxygen. The fish suffocate. They aren't poisoned.

scenes.heading: Biomagnification
scenes.question: Pesticide in a river food chain: algae 0.02 ppm, small fish 0.4, large fish 2, sea eagle 10 ppm. How many times more in the eagle?
scenes.say: Some chemicals, like DDT and mercury, build up the food chain. Here, a pesticide is at zero point zero two parts per million in algae, but ten in a sea eagle. That's five hundred times more. It's stored in fat, not excreted, and each predator eats many prey.
scenes.caption: Some chemicals, like DDT and mercury, build up the food chain. Here, a pesticide is at 0.02 ppm in algae, but 10 ppm in a sea eagle. That's 500 times more. It's stored in fat, not excreted, and each predator eats many prey.

scenes.heading: Climate change
points: Timing of breeding and flowering shifts
scenes.say: Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests add greenhouse gases that trap heat. When water stays too warm, corals expel the algae that feed them and turn white. That's coral bleaching. Species also shift to cooler places, and extreme weather increases.

scenes.heading: Conservation
scenes.say: Conservation strategies include protected areas, wildlife corridors, replanting native plants, and pest control, including biological control like the myxoma virus against rabbits. Captive breeding has helped species like the helmeted honeyeater.

Quick recap. Habitat loss, introduced species, pollution and climate change are the big threats. Fragmentation cuts genetic diversity, and chemicals biomagnify. Conservation helps. Now try the practice questions!
